newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal sees more Portucel sold this year.
newsitem.headline: Portugal sees more Portucel sold this year.

text.p: Portugal intends to sell a further stake of pulpmaker Portucel Industrial this year in a sector restructuring in which Britain's Arjo Wiggins could play a key role, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said on Tuesday.

The restructuring should involve Soporcel-Sociedade Portuguesa de Papel, Portucel Industrial-Empresa Produtora de Celulose, along with other companies from the Portucel group, and Inapa-Investimento, Participacoes and Gestao.
Portucel is 60 percent state-owned with the remainder on the market. Arjo has 43.5 percent of Soporcel, with state savings bank Caixa Geral de Depositos having 50.5 percent.
"I think that Arjo Wiggins...could be part of a complex business structure...with the sufficient degree of coordination and centralisation to be successful," Mateus said.

The economy ministry will receive on Wednesday various studies ordered from investment banks on the future of the Portuguese pulp and paper sector with the aim of bringing about greater integration between the paper and pulp operations.
